cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: tending what's growing, without forcing it
cells.place: at the threshold where what's been outside is arriving now
cells.ask: Offer this balance one thing to feed next: let go of one finished thing on purpose, the way a grown thing lets go of its own seed — release as the completion, not the loss. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust you, room held open without a hand closed around it.
cells.core: You're tending something that's arriving, and your hands are open while you do it. You give it what it needs — light, patience, the right amount of room — and you let it take the shape it's going to take. That's why it's actually growing, and why you're not worn thin by it.
cells.sheetLine: You're growing something without gripping it.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: managing what's growing, ahead of it
cells.place: at a threshold you're already standing past, meeting what hasn't arrived yet
cells.ask: There's no forcing the next step into view, so take the one that's actually lit: move through the not-knowing without demanding the whole road. What comes back, once the picture has been lived instead of pre-written, is care that doesn't exhaust — holding space without clutching.
cells.core: You're caring for something before it's here — planning its growth, guarding against every way it could go wrong, staying a step ahead so nothing catches you out. The care is real. It's also arriving ahead of the thing it's for, and the one holding it is the one running out of breath.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying what isn't here yet, and calling it care.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.place: at the threshold where what's arriving is waiting to be met
cells.ask: Don't force care into an empty room. Put your energy into what actually draws you — the star you'd steer by if you were honest about it — and let that pull bring the current back. What comes back when this side of you is warm again is care that doesn't exhaust, room held without clutching.
cells.core: Things around you could grow and you're not tending any of them. Not cruelty — distance, kept clean and called independence. Something back there made reaching feel like a cost, and you stopped paying it. Nothing you started has been allowed to become much yet.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing's growing because you stopped tending anything.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.place: at the threshold where what's arriving is being met — by you, largely unnoticed
cells.ask: The role got handed to you; the choosing didn't. Take it back down to its simplest form: let go, on purpose, of one thing you never agreed to carry — not as defeat, as clearing. What comes back when the grip opens is care that doesn't exhaust you, space held without clutching.
cells.core: People are being tended around you, and it's your doing — the meals, the remembering, the steadiness they lean on. You'd say you were just being practical, or just there. Meanwhile the care is running constantly and the one giving it feels emptied by it, without connecting the two.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one caring for everyone, and you call it nothing.
